title: Fictional fixture: retention of vessel navigation histories

period.label: 2080 navigation-data hearing
period.note: The invented hearing record is dated 2080.

context.statement: The navigation service stores identity-linked approach histories after a vessel leaves the harbor.

actors.label: Fictional Harbor Navigation Service
actors.role: Uses retained histories to personalize routing warnings.

actors.label: Fictional Mariner Privacy Coalition
actors.role: Demands purpose limits, deletion, and reviewable authorization.

formulations.text: Under what conditions did retained navigation history become an object of harbor governance?
formulations.researcher_note: This analytic formulation organizes the fixture for comparison; no actor uses this exact historical-emergence wording.

vocabulary.meaning_in_context: An identity-linked record of a vessel's prior routes and warnings.
The fixture author's umbrella label for otherwise separate retention, authorization, and deletion formulations.
vocabulary.provenance_note: No fictional actor uses this phrase; it exists only to demonstrate how a researcher label remains visible in the data.

institutions.label: Fictional Harbor Navigation Platform
institutions.role: Collects, retains, and applies vessel histories to later routing decisions.

stakes.statement: Participants oppose personalization and accident review to privacy, purpose limitation, and the ability to erase identity-linked histories.

presuppositions.statement: The dispute presupposes that records remain attributable and usable after the immediate navigation event.

accepted.statement: Retain histories for accident review under a fixed deletion deadline.

marginal.statement: Let each vessel inspect and revoke its own history immediately after departure.

answer_space.scope_note: No unthinkable answer is inferred from silence in the hearing.

competing_formulations.text: How much history is needed to issue safer warnings on a vessel's next visit?
Who authorizes reuse of a vessel's movements after the voyage for which they were collected?

sources.citation: Fictional Harbor Data Commission, Navigation-History Hearing (2080).
Fictional Harbor Navigation Service, Platform Lineage Note (2080).

evidence.excerpt: The Commission opens this navigation-history hearing on 4 May 2080.
Approach histories remain linked to vessel identity for ten years and shape warnings on later visits.
evidence.interpretation: Establishes durable identity-linked retention as the immediate object.

evidence.excerpt: Without the earlier routes we cannot personalize shallow-water warnings or compare a new anomaly to prior approaches.
evidence.interpretation: Provides the service's safety and personalization formulation.

evidence.excerpt: A navigation authorization is not permission for indefinite reuse; every later purpose requires a public rule and a deletion right.
Proposals include a two-year accident-review window, immediate vessel-controlled deletion, and ten-year service retention.
evidence.interpretation: Bounds the documented retention answer space.

evidence.excerpt: The present platform descends technically from the shared signal-control network installed in 1949.
evidence.interpretation: Supports infrastructure succession but does not itself establish problem continuity.

evidence.excerpt: The note lists hardware and protocol predecessors but names no earlier debate about control authority.
evidence.interpretation: Limits the strength of historical recognition evidence; absence in one note is not proof of no lineage elsewhere.

hindsight_risks.description: A researcher may collapse distinct safety, authorization, and deletion formulations into the modern umbrella label privacy.
hindsight_risks.mitigation: Preserve the umbrella as researcher_analytic and retain the actors' competing formulations separately.

uncertainties.description: Technical descent from the 1949 network does not prove that the 2080 actors inherited its problem formulation.
uncertainties.mitigation: Keep the cross-episode relation undetermined pending evidence of debate transmission.
